Lessons.Title: Using Quadratic Expressions in Vertex Form to Solve Problems
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: use vertex form to find extrema in a real-world quadratic optimization model and solve a specified target value, carefully interpreting symmetry and feasible domains. Independently authored Edulytiks adaptation of Illustrative Mathematics Algebra 1 First Edition Unit 7 Lesson 23 teacher https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/7/23/preparation.html and student https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/students/1/7/23/index.html (CC BY 4.0). The publisher applies complete-square representations to decisions, not merely symbols.

Original fenced rectangle: 40 metres of perimeter with width w metres and length20−w metres. Allowed widths 0≤w≤20 for a limiting mathematical model and 0<w<20 for non-degenerate rectangles. Area A(w)=w(20−w)=20w−w²=100−(w−10)² square metres. Maximum100m² at w10m and complementary length10m.

Target area84m² yields 100−(w−10)²=84, so (w−10)²=16 and w=6 or14. Both represent dimensions6m×14m, merely exchanging width/length, and are within the physical domain. The solutions need not correspond to two distinct rectangle shapes.

Student task: sketch feasible widths, convert area to vertex form, find largest area, solve target84 and explain equivalence of two dimension orderings. Teacher-scored rubric0–2 for context/units, vertex derivation, valid root interpretation and critique of treating negative/degenerate dimensions as physical rectangles.
